chunks: Even if We had sent you a transcript on paper which they could feel with their hands, the unbelievers would have said: 'This is nothing but clear sorcery.'

key_terms.الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا: The disbelievers/those who cover the truth
key_terms.قِرْطَاسٍ: A sheet of paper or parchment

ai.seo_question: Why would disbelievers still reject the Quran even if it were a physical book they could touch?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse (6:7) is often linked to the concept of *'illat al-kufr* (the cause of disbelief), illustrating that the Qurayh's rejection was rooted in spiritual arrogance rather than a deficit of empirical proof. The mention of 'paper' (*qirṭās*) emphasizes the tangible nature of the revelation, yet their claim of 'clear magic' (*sihr mubin*) reveals a cognitive dissonance where they dismissed divine truth as sorcery to preserve their ego. This underscores the Shia scholarly view that guidance requires not just evidence, but the humility to accept it.
